# `silk/geometry/point`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Two- and three-dimensional positions over any number type.

## When to use
Use [`Point2`](#Point2) or [`Point3`](#Point3) for a location, such as a path vertex, a glyph outline point, or
the corner of a box. Use `silk.geometry.vector` for a displacement between locations.

## Details
A point is a `Copy` struct with public fields, generic over its number type `T`. Point
arithmetic keeps positions and displacements apart: `point - point` gives a vector, `point +
vector` and `point - vector` give a point, and there is no `point + point`. `&a == &b` compares
every field when `T: Equal`. Methods appear only when `T` has the operations they need:
`distance` needs `silk.num.numeric.Float`.

## Gotchas
Comparison takes shared borrows, as in `&a == &b`. Float fields compare with IEEE rules, so a
point with a NaN field is not equal to itself.

## Examples
### Move a point and measure how far it went
```silk
import silk.geometry.point { Point2 }
import silk.geometry.vector { Vector2 }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let start = Point2<f64>.new(1.0, 1.0)
  let end = start + Vector2<f64>.new(3.0, 4.0)
  let offset = end - start
  if start.distance(end) != 5.0 || offset.x != 3.0 || start.midpoint(end).y != 3.0 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Point2` with `import silk.geometry.point { Point2 }`.

## `Point2`

```silk
pub struct Point2<T>
```

A position in a plane with an `x` and a `y` coordinate of number type `T`.

### When to use

Use `Point2` for a location. Use `silk.geometry.vector.Vector2` for a displacement.

### Details

The fields are public. `point - point` gives a `Vector2<T>`, and `point + vector` and `point -
vector` give a `Point2<T>`, when `T` has the operator. There is no `point + point`. `&a == &b`
compares both coordinates when `T: Equal`.

<a id="Point2.x"></a>

### Field `x`

```silk
pub x: T
```

The horizontal coordinate.

<a id="Point2.y"></a>

### Field `y`

```silk
pub y: T
```

The vertical coordinate. In a y-down space, such as SVG or a screen, `y` grows downward.

## `Point3`

```silk
pub struct Point3<T>
```

A position in space with `x`, `y`, and `z` coordinates of number type `T`.

### When to use

Use `Point3` for a location in space, such as a point that a `silk.geometry.matrix.Matrix4`
projects. Use `silk.geometry.vector.Vector3` for a displacement.

### Details

The fields are public. `point - point` gives a `Vector3<T>`, and `point + vector` and `point -
vector` give a `Point3<T>`, when `T` has the operator. There is no `point + point`. `&a == &b`
compares all three coordinates when `T: Equal`.

<a id="Point3.x"></a>

### Field `x`

```silk
pub x: T
```

The first coordinate.

<a id="Point3.y"></a>

### Field `y`

```silk
pub y: T
```

The second coordinate.

<a id="Point3.z"></a>

### Field `z`

```silk
pub z: T
```

The third coordinate.
